subject: Running Distance under Linux or Mac

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Running Distance under Linux or Mac
parts:
Distance-sampling list:

In response to a user question, I have updated the section of the Distance
support page that deals with how to run Distance from other operating systems
(a copy below, without all the hyperlinks). Also, Distance 5 includes a
library for the free, multiplatform software R that fits single and double
observer distance sampling data (but without adjustment terms for the single-
platform detection function at present). Although this library has only been
tested in R for Windows, it may well run under other operating systems
(possibly with some minor tweaking - let us know if you try it).

If anyone has any more information to contribute on this topic, please email
me! Thanks,

- Len Thomas

Linux: Although we don't have any direct experience, Distance should run
without problems within the emulation software VMWare or win4lin. For VMWare,
note that there is a free version called VMWare player, and if you search the
web under something like "Free VMWare" you will find instructions about how to
set up operating system images using free software (one site is
http://johnbokma.com/vmware-player/). Other possibilities are to use the free
emulators Bochs (pronounced "box" - slow, apparently) or QEMU (with the
accelerator module). For up to date information, try searching the web for
"PC Emulators" or "PC Virtualizers". If you try any of these solutions,
please let us know how you get on!

Apple Macintosh: Distance 3.5 and Distance 4.0 were tested on a G4 PowerMac
running Virtual PC (since acquired by Microsoft) and both ran without
problems, although both run quite slowly and Distance 4 especially needs quite
a bit of memory. Other emulators will probably work as well - see
http://www.macwindows.com/emulator.html for a list and latest news. If you
try any, then let us know how they work.
